#### Q2 — status: answered

**Question:** Is this object Lead, Opportunity, Solution, or Case?

**Why it matters:** Those four require a businessProcess; every other object forbids one, and both mistakes are deploy failures.

**Answer shape:** The object name, and whether a BusinessProcess file must ship with the record type.

**From skill:** `admin/record-types-and-page-layouts`

**Proposed default:** Case — so a Support Process must be authored and deployed alongside every Case record type.

Answer: Case. The requirement is written entirely in terms of Case creation, case numbers and case ownership ("Within the first minute of a case being created..."), so a Support Process (BusinessProcess) must be authored and deployed alongside every Case record type.

### access

#### Q7 — status: answered

**Question:** What is on the current profile that has no permission-set equivalent?

**Why it matters:** loginHours, loginIpRanges, layoutAssignments, the default app and the default record type exist only on Profile. They are the residue, and the only reason a profile still exists.

**Who can answer:** Security architect

**Answer shape:** The residue list — the exact contents of the base profile file.

**From skill:** `admin/permission-sets-vs-profiles`

**Proposed default:** A minimal base profile per team carrying only layout assignments, default app and default record type; every object, field and tab grant lives in permission sets.

Answer: A minimal base profile per team carrying only layout assignments, default app and default record type; every object, field and tab grant lives in permission sets. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q8 — status: answered

**Question:** Which users hold this profile, and do they all hold the same user licence?

**Why it matters:** A permission set with a LicenseId can only be assigned where the profile's UserLicenseId matches; a mixed-licence population must be split before, not after.

**Who can answer:** Security architect

**Answer shape:** The population split by licence, and whether LicenseId should be left empty.

**From skill:** `admin/permission-sets-vs-profiles`

**Proposed default:** 18 internal users (12 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 2 Billing) on Salesforce licences with Service Cloud; leave LicenseId empty on the permission sets.

Answer: 18 internal users split 12 Tier 1 / 4 Tier 2 / 2 Billing (per requirement's team counts), all on Salesforce licences with Service Cloud (per requirement: "We are moving to Service Cloud"); leave LicenseId empty on the permission sets (default accepted for that design decision — dry run).

Answer: Additive — this is a new Service Cloud footprint, so every grant is new and no strip phase is required. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q11 — status: answered

### routing

#### Q15 — status: answered

**Question:** Which channels create cases, at what steady-state volume, and what is the biggest single batch anyone would ever push?

**Why it matters:** Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual entry have different limits, routing behaviour and spam exposure; and automation that passes UAT on ten records fails on a bulk load, because Flow and Apex share the transaction limits.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** A channel inventory with the daily limit and pending-queue risk for each, plus a steady-state number and a worst-case batch number.

**From skill:** `admin/case-management-setup`

**Proposed default:** Email-to-Case ~400/day (support@ and billing@), Web-to-Case ~60/day, manual ~20/day, no phone; no bulk Case load is planned, so the worst-case batch is the daily email peak.

Answer: Email-to-Case ~400/day (support@acme.example and billing@acme.example combined), Web-to-Case ~60/day, manual agent entry ~20/day, no phone channel (per requirement). No bulk Case load is planned, so the worst-case batch is the daily email peak (~400).

#### Q16 — status: answered

**Question:** What must happen in the first minute: owner, acknowledgement, calendar, priority?

**Why it matters:** Assignment, auto-response, business hours and priority all resolve during the save; anything set later runs on the wrong clock.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** The before-save Flow scope and the assignment-rule design, stated as an ordered list of what happens during the save.

**From skill:** `admin/case-management-setup`

**Proposed default:** All four in the first minute: assignment rule sets the owner, auto-response sends the acknowledgement with the case number, a before-save Flow stamps Case.BusinessHoursId, and priority is mapped from the form field or the mailbox.

Answer: All four in the first minute, per requirement: an owner is assigned, the customer receives an acknowledgement with the case number, the SLA clock is running on the right calendar, and priority is set from what the form or email tells us.

Per the proposed default, assume each forwards to exactly one Salesforce routing address (default accepted — dry run for that specific claim); confirm with IT before go-live that neither mailbox has a second forwarding rule.

**Question:** Who maintains next year's holidays, and when?

**Why it matters:** Holidays expire; unmaintained calendars silently stop pausing.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** An owner and a yearly deploy slot in the release calendar.

**From skill:** `admin/business-hours-and-holidays`

**Proposed default:** A named owner in Service Operations, with a yearly holiday deploy booked in the release calendar each Q4.

Answer: A named owner in Service Operations, with a yearly holiday deploy booked in the release calendar each Q4. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q91 — status: answered

**Question:** How will we know next month that the escalation rule still fires?

**Why it matters:** IsEscalated is a plain writable boolean, not an engine-owned lock — nothing reports on a rule that quietly stopped.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** A saved report or query on escalated, still-open cases, with an owner and a cadence.

**From skill:** `admin/escalation-rules`

**Proposed default:** A saved report on escalated, still-open Cases, reviewed weekly by the Tier 2 lead.

Answer: A saved report on escalated, still-open Cases, reviewed weekly by the Tier 2 lead. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q92 — status: deferred

**Question:** Is entitlement versioning on, and who owns the next version?

**Why it matters:** The version fields do nothing until the org switch is on, and an SLA change means a new file with every time-trigger offset re-derived.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** The versioning switch state and a named owner for version bumps.

**From skill:** `admin/entitlements-and-milestones`

Answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

### validation

#### Q93 — status: answered

**Question:** Does each message fit in 255 characters and name both the problem and the fix?

**Why it matters:** errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that cannot say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence.

**Who can answer:** CRM admin lead

**Answer shape:** The final message text per rule, under 255 characters, naming both the problem and the fix.

**From skill:** `admin/validation-rules`

**Proposed default:** Write the final message text at design time, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time.

Answer: Write the final message text at design time, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time. (default accepted — dry run)

### testing-and-environments

#### Q94 — status: answered

**Question:** Who owns each environment, and who approves its refresh?

**Why it matters:** An environment with no owner is the one that gets refreshed over someone's uncommitted work.

**Who can answer:** Release manager

**Answer shape:** A named owner per environment, and a separate named approver for its refresh.

**From skill:** `admin/sandbox-strategy`

**Proposed default:** A named owner per row of the topology table, with the data owner (not the refresher) accountable for approving a refresh.

Answer: A named owner per row of the topology table, with the data owner (not the refresher) accountable for approving a refresh. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q95 — status: deferred

**Question:** When must the validation deploy run relative to sign-off, and who accepts a deferred defect?

**Why it matters:** A quick deploy only skips tests within 10 days of a successful validation, so a validation taken at the start of a three-week cycle is dead by sign-off.

**Who can answer:** Release manager

**Answer shape:** A dated validation slot in the plan, and a named business owner for the known-issues list.

**From skill:** `admin/uat-and-acceptance-criteria`

Answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

#### Q96 — status: answered

**Question:** Which permission set or group carries the feature, and is its recalculation finished?

**Why it matters:** PermissionSetGroup.Status is a real picklist — Outdated or Updating means the tester does not yet have what the script assumes.

**Who can answer:** CRM admin lead

**Answer shape:** A pre-run gate query, and the PSG each persona depends on.

**From skill:** `admin/uat-test-case-design`

**Proposed default:** A pre-run gate query on PermissionSetGroup.Status before each UAT session, so a false-fail is not logged as a build defect.

Answer: A pre-run gate query on PermissionSetGroup.Status before each UAT session, so a false-fail is not logged as a build defect. (default accepted — dry run)

#### Q97 — status: answered

**Question:** When a test case fails, who decides Fail versus Blocked?

**Why it matters:** Blocked is an environment result and must not raise a defect against the build; conflating them corrupts the defect data.

**Who can answer:** Process owner

**Answer shape:** A named triager and a re-runnable run sheet.

**From skill:** `admin/uat-test-case-design`

**Proposed default:** A named triager (the QA or BA lead) with a run sheet whose rows are re-runnable rather than overwritten.

Answer: A named triager (the QA or BA lead) with a run sheet whose rows are re-runnable rather than overwritten. (default accepted — dry run)
